image_description: A red lionfish (Pterois volitans) swimming near a rocky, algae-covered seabed. The fish displays characteristic vertical reddish-brown and white stripes, large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays, and prominent dorsal spines. The lighting is somewhat dim, typical of underwater photography, with some particulate matter in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head structure is visible; the eye is distinct and the mouth shape aligns with scorpaenid morphology, though partially obscured by angle and lighting.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed body with moderately sized proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears laterally compressed as expected for a lionfish, viewed from a slight angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct vertical bands of reddish-brown and white are clearly visible on the body and fins.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pelvic fins also with elongated spines.

artifact_observations.location: Pectoral fin edges and background interface
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness and 'haloing' around the finest tips of the pectoral fin rays where they meet the darker background, suggestive of minor generative blur or compression artifacts common in AI underwater scenes.

The caudal fin (tail) lacks clear definition of individual rays compared to the pectorals; it appears somewhat fused or melted into the background turbulence, lacking the crisp structural integrity of the front fins.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification (Pterois volitans/miles) and rule out generic fish hallucinations.
To audit the connectivity of the delicate fin rays and ensure they don't merge incorrectly with the background or each other.
To assess the realism of the underwater lighting, particulate matter, and overall texture consistency.

focus_areas: Integrity of dorsal and pectoral fin rays (no fusion/melting)
Clarity of stripe patterns on the body
Structural definition of the caudal (tail) fin
Boundary separation between translucent fins and dark background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the caudal fin (tail). In many AI-generated fish images, the tail dissolves or lacks ray structure. Verify if the 'texture_anomaly' on the fin edges is actual generative failure or just depth-of-field blur. Ensure the dorsal spines are individually distinct and not fused at the base.
